claims.text: THE ARCHIVE ITEM IS MISTITLED AND THE BOARD SHOULD SAY SO. The archive.org item is captioned 'Malmstrom Air Force Base Incident - March 16, 1967 NORAD logs'. Its contents are the 24th NORAD Region Senior Director's Log for 7 to 19 November 1975 and it contains nothing about 16 March 1967. Anyone citing this item for the 1967 Echo Flight incident is citing the wrong document.

claims.text: The log records its own negatives as readily as its sightings: after the 7 Nov 1327Z entry, 'all this time, surveillance has not been able to detect any sort of track except for known traffic'; on 9 Nov at 0320Z the FAA watch supervisor reporting United Flight 157 seeing a meteor; and on 12 Nov at 0251Z 'Never had any joy (contact) on radar.' Its final entry is marked in the original as the last pertaining to these incidents.

desc: A WORKING OPERATIONAL LOG, WHICH IS WHY IT IS WORTH MORE THAN ANY REPORT. The 24th NORAD Region Senior Director's Log at Malmstrom AFB records thirteen days of reports from the 341st Strategic Missile Wing's field in the controllers' own shorthand, timed in Zulu, with site designators, radar track numbers, height-finder readings and aircraft call-outs. It was released under FOIA over the signature block 'TERRENCE C. JAMES, Colonel, USAF, Director of Administration', with copies to HQ USAF/DAD and HQ USAF/JACL, and the extracted pages carry stamps 450, 451 and 452 plus a control number 000974, showing that it is a fragment of a much larger paginated release. The log is not an advocate's document and does not read like one: alongside the sightings it records that surveillance could detect no track except known traffic, that an airline crew reported a meteor, and that on 12 November the controllers never had any contact on radar at all. It also contains the 10 November entry naming Minot Air Force Station rather than Minot AFB, which is the one unresolved naming problem in the 1975 sequence. NOTE THE ARCHIVE ITEM IS MISTITLED: it is filed as 'Malmstrom Air Force Base Incident - March 16, 1967 NORAD logs' and its contents are the November 1975 log.

timeline.label: The NORAD log closes the Malmstrom sequence
timeline.text: '19 Nov 75 (1327Z) - SAC command post report UFO observed by FSC & a cook, observed object travelling NE between M-8 and M-l at a fast rate of speed. Object bright white light seen 45 to 50 sec following terrain 200 ft off ground. The light was two to three times brighter than landing lights on a jet.' The original marks this as the last entry pertaining to these incidents.

unverified: The remaining pages of the FOIA compilation from which this log was extracted. At least 449 pages have never been seen by this board, and they are the same release stream that produced the Loring, Wurtsmith, Falconbridge and Cannon material.

The text is OCR of a scan and carries transcription artefacts throughout, including 'M-l' for M-1 and 'L-l' for L-1. Quotations on this board preserve the artefacts rather than silently correcting them.
